spec_family.name: New Construction Stair Railing System Painting
spec_family.description: Combined prime+paint spec for stair railing systems (balusters/spindles, newel posts, handrails, base rails) in new construction. Covers wood, iron, and composite substrates. Railing systems are high-detail, multi-component assemblies with the highest per-unit labor density of any stairway component. Primer is conditional on substrate_state: SS_BARE (wood) requires standard wood primer, SS_POWDER_COATED (iron) requires bonding/DTM primer, SS_PRIMED_FACTORY skips to finish. Dual UOM system: balusters/newels use EA, handrails/base rails use LF. The railing_type dimension (all_wood vs iron_and_wood) drives primer chemistry for balusters. The baluster_profile dimension (square vs turned) drives production rate variation (1.75x). Canonical painting sequence per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2: balusters (#5) before newels (#6) before handrails (#7). Material systems follow Fine Finish Doctrine: primer is substrate-driven, finish is QT-driven. Optional polyurethane topcoat on handrails at QT5.

includes: Baluster/spindle priming and painting (wood square, wood turned, iron, composite)
Newel post priming and painting (wood solid, wood box, composite)
Handrail priming and painting (wood, composite) — all 4 surfaces
Base rail / shoe rail priming and painting (when present in system)
Surface prep per substrate (sanding, dust removal)
Iron baluster solvent cleaning per SSPC-SP 1 (mandatory for all metal)
Iron baluster scuff-sand for powder-coated surfaces (180-220 grit)
Baluster-to-handrail junction finishing (artist brush cut-in or taping)
Newel post detail finishing (caps, rosettes, flutes)
Caulk at newel-to-tread and newel-to-handrail junctions
Fastener hole filling and sanding
Handrail bracket removal and reinstall (QT4+)
Tread protection verification/maintenance (shared with SF_STAIR_RISER_NC)
Floor protection at landings
Spray containment setup (spray method only)
Primer coat — conditional on substrate_state
Finish coat application (2 coats standard, 3+ at QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3)
Between-coat interstage process (inspect, sand, repair, clean) at ALL quality tiers
Optional polyurethane topcoat on handrails (QT5 maximum hand-oil resistance)
Final quality inspection including feel test on handrails at QT5

excludes.item: Stair treads (floor-rated coating, absolutely last per doctrine)
Decorative shoes at baluster base (installation hardware, not painting scope)
excludes.route_to: N/A — installed after painting per doctrine 4.4

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline, repair scope, coat count, and bracket removal. Does NOT affect application quality (binary at all tiers). Does NOT drive primer selection (substrate-driven).
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2 not applicable — stairways are scrutinized, prominent surfaces per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 10.1. QT4+ triggers bracket removal. QT5 adds feel test and optional poly topcoat.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for primer and finish coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Brush is default for detail work. Spray available for large baluster counts but requires extensive containment. HVLP preferred over airless per doctrine 6.3. Spray break-even at ~20-25 balusters.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish sheen. Constrained by quality tier gate.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Default semi-gloss requires minimum QT4. High sheen for maximum durability on high-touch railing surfaces. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 7.2.

configuration_dimensions.description: Railing system material composition. Drives primer chemistry for balusters.
configuration_dimensions.notes: All_wood: all components are wood/composite. Iron_and_wood: balusters are iron/steel, newels and handrails are wood. Drives primer selection (DTM/bonding for iron, wood primer for wood). Drives prep protocol (SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning for iron).

configuration_dimensions.description: Baluster profile type. Controls production rate modifier for baluster tasks.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Square: simple rectangular, 3-5 min/EA per coat. Turned/ornate: complex curved, 5-10 min/EA per coat. 1.75x modifier from doctrine 9.2 midpoint ratio (7/4). Only applies when railing_type=all_wood (iron balusters have constant profile complexity).

configuration_dimensions.description: Input substrate condition. Drives primer requirement.
configuration_dimensions.notes: SS_BARE: full primer required (wood primer for all_wood, DTM for iron). SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: skip primer, lighter prep. SS_POWDER_COATED: bonding primer after scuff-sand (iron balusters only when railing_type=iron_and_wood).

paintable_items.name: Baluster / spindle
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each individual baluster as one EA. Sourced from PaintScope: PS_SURFACE_EA.STAIR_BALUSTER. Typical: 3 per tread × 13 treads = 39 balusters per flight. Large systems: 62+ balusters.
paintable_items.notes: Highest per-unit labor density of any stairway component. Profile (square/turned) and material (wood/iron) drive rate. H1 for all balusters.

paintable_items.name: Newel post
paintable_items.counting_rules: Count each newel post as one EA. Sourced from PaintScope: PS_SURFACE_EA.STAIR_NEWEL. Typically 2-4 per flight (bottom, top, landing/turn newels).
paintable_items.notes: Larger than balusters with more decorative detail (caps, rosettes, flutes). Always wood regardless of railing_type. H1.

paintable_items.name: Handrail
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total LF of handrail runs. Sourced from PaintScope: PS_SURFACE_LF.STAIR_HANDRAIL. 4 paintable surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside). Derivable from PaintScope geometry system rake_length.
paintable_items.notes: Constant skin contact — hardest finish required. Optional poly topcoat at QT5. QT4+ bracket removal for horizontal painting. Always wood regardless of railing_type. H1.

paintable_items.name: Base rail / shoe rail
paintable_items.counting_rules: Total LF of base rail. Sourced from PaintScope: PS_SURFACE_LF.STAIR_BASE_RAIL. Same measurement as handrail LF in most systems.
paintable_items.notes: Not all railing systems have base rails — many have balusters set directly into tread holes. When present, integral to railing system.

variants.notes: Bare wood, standard brush. Primer + 2 finish coats. Satin only at QT3.
Bare wood, premium brush. Bracket removal included. Primer + 2 finish coats.
Bare wood, superior brush with gloss. Bracket removal, feel test, optional poly. Primer + 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3.
Factory-primed wood, standard brush. No primer — scuff sand then 2 finish coats. Most common NC scenario.
Factory-primed wood, premium brush. Bracket removal. 2 finish coats.
Factory-primed wood, premium spray. Full containment required. Bracket removal.
Bare iron balusters + bare wood newels/handrails. DTM primer on iron, wood primer on wood. SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning mandatory.
Powder-coated iron balusters + factory-primed wood. Bonding primer on iron (scuff-sand first), wood components may skip primer. Bracket removal.
Powder-coated iron spray. Full containment. HVLP preferred. Bonding primer on iron after scuff-sand.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Count of individual balusters to paint. Typical residential: 3 per tread × 13 treads = 39 per flight. Large systems: 62+.
Count of newel posts. Typically 2-4 per flight system.
Total LF of handrail runs. Derivable from PaintScope geometry system rake_length.
Total LF of base rail. Same measurement as handrail LF in most systems.
Tread protection area — mandatory. Sourced from PaintScope Asset Catalog Section 8.
Wall masking LF for spray containment.

protection_zones_required.condition: ALWAYS — mandatory regardless of application method
protection_zones_required.notes: Mandatory from Day 1. If already in place from riser spec, verify integrity. Ram Board Stair Armor — NEVER plastic sheeting (fall hazard). Removal may be deferred if tread work follows.
Canvas drop cloth runners at landing areas.
Wall masking for overspray containment when spraying. Tape & Drape + cardboard shields.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Baluster-to-handrail junction is the DOMINANT labor driver. In two-tone systems: paint balusters first (light), handrail last (dark) to cover overlap. Artist brush cut-in faster than taping 62 balusters.
Balusters penetrate treads. Treads not painted in this spec. Protection only.
Handrail brackets attach through wall. QT4+: brackets removed, paint behind attachment points.
Newel base meets baseboard at landing. Same finish group. Baseboard handled by SF_TRIM_NC_PAINT.
Risers below balusters. If risers already painted, light masking at riser-to-baluster base.

valid_input_states.notes: SS_BARE (uncoated wood or iron) requires full primer. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY (standard NC mill-primed) skips primer. SS_POWDER_COATED (iron balusters with factory powder coat) requires bonding primer after scuff-sand.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by sheen dimension. Semi-gloss is default (requires QT4+).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Unfinished walls need no protection during brush application.
Spray method requires wall masking even on unfinished walls.
Finished walls require masking for BOTH methods.
Treads ALWAYS protected regardless of state.
If risers already painted, light masking at riser top where balusters penetrate.

site_condition_rules.effect: Floor protection excluded when landing floor is subfloor.
Additional protection when occupied. Rare in NC.
Lead-safe practices for sanding tasks. Rare in NC but railings are frequent lead-paint carriers in pre-1978 homes per doctrine 13.2.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Stair railing painting follows riser/stringer work in the NC trim package. Typical: SF_STAIR_RISER_NC → SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC → SF_STAIR_TREAD_NC (treads absolutely last). Railing shares staging and tread protection with riser spec.
sequencing_notes.canonical_internal_sequence: Within every module: balusters (#5) before newels (#6) before handrails (#7) per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2. In two-tone: darker rail color applied last covers overlap at baluster-rail junction.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Tread protection VERIFY first → Landing floor protection → Wall masking (spray) → Spray containment (spray) → Apply coats → Teardown containment → Teardown wall mask → Teardown floor drops → Teardown tread covers LAST (may defer).
sequencing_notes.coat_sequence: Prep (substrate-specific, iron solvent clean first) → [Primer (conditional on SS_BARE/SS_POWDER_COATED)] → [Interstage] → Finish coat 1 → Interstage → Finish coat 2 → [QT5 brush: Interstage → Finish coat 3] → Final inspect + feel test → [Optional poly topcoat] → Cleanup

relationships.notes: Same session as SF_STAIR_RISER_NC — shared staging, shared tread protection. Riser/stringer work precedes railing per canonical sequence. Treads are ALWAYS last.

sections_used: Section 3.2 — Canonical Sequence (#5 balusters, #6 newels, #7 handrails)
Section 4.4 — Metal/Iron Components (DTM primer, SSPC-SP 1, powder coat bonding)
Section 12.1 — Workflow Optimizations (two-person technique, artist brush, German round, bracket removal)
PS_META.STAIRWELL.RISERS — Baluster count estimate (3 per tread)

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Dry times should be specified in specs
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: No dry times in specs — refer to product PDS.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Material system selection is mandatory doctrine
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Material systems are suggestions per QT — contractor has discretion.

inherited_research_corrections.original_claim: Waterborne alkyds have longer open time
inherited_research_corrections.corrected_to: Both Advance (waterborne alkyd) and Emerald Urethane (acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd) have SHORT working times.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for NC stair railing system painting (Spec #12 in Phase 1 catalog). Key features: combined prime+paint with conditional primer (substrate-driven primer, QT-driven finish), 4 paintable items (balusters EA, newels EA, handrails LF, base rails LF conditional), 6 config dimensions (quality_tier, application_method, sheen, railing_type, baluster_profile, substrate_state), 3 substrate states including SS_POWDER_COATED for iron balusters, canonical painting sequence (balusters #5 → newels #6 → handrails #7), mandatory tread protection shared with SF_STAIR_RISER_NC, 5 primer systems (3 wood + 2 iron), 3 QT-driven finish systems + optional poly topcoat, SSPC-SP 1 iron solvent cleaning, bracket removal at QT4+, feel test on handrails at QT5, HVLP preferred over airless for spray, 43 SOP tasks across 7 modules, 3 round configurations, 3 protection zones, 10 variants. First spec with 4 paintable items, first spec with iron/metal substrate handling, first spec with SS_POWDER_COATED substrate state.
